extracted.intended_audience: general newspaper readers and the wartime public (readers of Associated Press dispatches); also relevant to policymakers referenced in the stories
extracted.subtask_description: Contemporaneous newspaper dispatches and briefs reporting Allied and Axis military actions, government and international-policy statements, and public-interest wartime issues (labor disputes, food policy, naval actions) during World War II.

rubrics_metrics.name: Observe the laws of humanity in aerial war
rubrics_metrics.description: Pope Pius XII urged the belligerents to respect the laws of humanity in the aerial war, exhorting them once more to observe these laws.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Pope warned against reprisals and the progressive application of means of strife that make no distinction between military and non-military objectives; he emphasized that moral judgments should not be biased simply because an action was taken by one party or the other and that attention must be paid to whether actions accord with right and the laws of humanity. He also expressed special concern for small nations and non-combatants who suffer disproportionately.

rubrics_metrics.name: No-strike pledge and compliance with War Labor Board directives (coal/mines)
rubrics_metrics.description: The War Labor Board stated that several hundred thousand workers were out on strike 'in violation of the "no strike" pledge' and in defiance of directive orders and an executive order placing the mines under Federal management.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The board framed the situation as a fundamental issue of the supremacy of law that 'must be met by the government.' It characterized the strike as a reckless disregard of wartime obligations and said the board stands ready to proceed with the case in accordance with its policies as soon as the strike is ended.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suspend negotiations while a party violates board orders
rubrics_metrics.description: The War Labor Board directed that all negotiations and proceedings referenced by its directive order of May 25 should cease until the mine workers return to work in compliance with the board's order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stated policy: 'no proceedings conducted under the auspices or direction of the board can be carried on while either party to a dispute stands in violation of the agreement.' The board sent telegrams to the parties and documented prior steps taken by the government, indicating federal action is contemplated if noncompliance continues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposed international 'yardstick' of diet (sample quantities)
rubrics_metrics.description: The United Nations food conference proposed a 'yardstick' diet: a well-fed citizen would consume between 228 and 250 quarts of milk and between 228 and 276 eggs every year, plus about 900 pounds of other foods selected according to their nutrition values.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The sample yardstick enumerates food groups (starch-rich tubers/roots/fruits; mature leguminous seeds and nuts; vitamin C–rich fruits; leafy/green/yellow vegetables; other vegetables and fruits; meats/fish/poultry; sugar and fats). Conference experts said the sample probably would have to be modified in various countries to meet existing economic and agricultural realities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Governments must provide for nutritionally vulnerable groups
rubrics_metrics.description: Conference report: 'each government must provide for its citizens whose need is greatest in proportion to their physiological needs however scarce or plentiful supplies of food may be.' Vulnerable groups named include expectant and nursing mothers, heavy workers, and low-income families.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The recommendation assigns governments primary responsibility to help less-fortunate citizens achieve the yardstick level and emphasizes priority distribution proportionate to physiological needs. The report noted wartime hardships and urged restoration or design of targeted public nutrition assistance and ration differentiation where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nutrition education and practical demonstration (schools and communal meals)
rubrics_metrics.description: The conference urged that 'simple facts about food and diet should be taught in all schools,' and that communal meals which are well prepared and of high nutritive value teach by force of example.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommended educational programs across nations to spread knowledge through communities so as to influence governmental action and activities of food suppliers; collective feeding arrangements were highlighted as making a great contribution to improving diets, industrial output, morale, and general health.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adapt dietary recommendations to local economic/agricultural realities
rubrics_metrics.description: Although the conference proposed a sample yardstick, it acknowledged 'the sample probably would have to be modified in various countries' and that 'innumerable combinations of individual foods may be devised' to meet the yardstick.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance is to devise local combinations of foods that meet nutritional goals while reflecting economic and agricultural conditions; flexibility in applying the yardstick is explicit rather than mandatory uniformity.
